review.purpose: Preserve exact-string cross-table equality while exposing incompatible token key versions.
review.finding: Aligned tokens preserve nine distinct matched orders and USD555. The fixed-v1 customer mapping matches nine orders under v1 but none when orders use v2; aligned mappings still match. Missing and unknown identifiers stay unmatched. This small-fixture reconciliation does not prove global token uniqueness or anonymization.

review.purpose: Separate a display value from a unique join key and quantify multiplicity inflation.
review.finding: Four of six customers share redacted display values. A deliberately incorrect display-value join retains nine distinct orders but produces 16 rows / USD 970, seven extra rows/USD415 above the reference. Redaction ignores token key versions, so that inflation stays fixed.

review.purpose: Separate selected-alphabet domain eligibility and visible transformation from successful recovery.
review.finding: The default digits profile changes two of eight present values and deliberately passes six below-minimum rows through; the ninth row remains NULL. Under alnum, five present values become eligible/changed and three pass through. Punctuation and length remain intact; preserved structure and deterministic output do not establish privacy.

review.purpose: Verify exact recovery with matching profile/key while detecting the misleading pass-through success case.
review.finding: All eight nonmissing inputs recover exactly under either digits or alnum, including rows that never changed. NULL remains missing. Ten independent accounting/shape/boundary checks pass; recovery is neither evidence of every input being transformed nor a production key-management test.
